elements.scope_reason: Red-box header: presenting complaint plus Urgent level
elements.problem: Encoded as (and <gum/teeth complaint> (or ...)) at Urgent, as the house standard asks. The complaint is a pair of grouper concepts (Tooth finding / Gingivae finding); see rule-level problems for whether a recorded Toothache or Bleeding gums will match them.
evidence: Urgent: gum/teeth symptoms with danger signs :: (and (or (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Tooth finding" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Gingivae finding" "finding"))) (or ...)) Urgent

elements.problem: Three parts (temperature >= 38 °C AND swelling of face / jaw / next to tooth) are all encoded with the right threshold, unit, direction and and/or structure. The swellings are in check_for and temperature is a routine vital.
evidence: Urgent: gum/teeth symptoms with danger signs :: (and (>= (measurement (snomed_concept "Body temperature" "observable entity") °C) 38) (or (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Facial swelling" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Swelling" "finding") (finding_site (snomed_concept "Jaw region structure" "body structure"))) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Swelling" "finding") (finding_site (snomed_concept "Tooth, gum, and/or supporting structure" "body structure")))))

elements.problem: Eat and drink are encoded as two OR'd findings, both checked for.
evidence: Urgent: gum/teeth symptoms with danger signs :: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Unable to eat" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Unable to drink" "finding"))

elements.problem: Both parts are OR'd. 'Felt without touching' is Toothache + Spontaneous, which is acceptable. 'Wakes patient at night' is Toothache + Night time: this loses the 'wakes from sleep' meaning (pain only at night would also match). A 'Night pain' (finding) concept exists but carries no tooth site, so the current choice is defensible. Minor.
evidence: Urgent: gum/teeth symptoms with danger signs :: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Toothache" "finding") (qualifier (snomed_concept "Spontaneous" "qualifier value"))) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Toothache" "finding") (qualifier (snomed_concept "Night time" "qualifier value")))

elements.scope_reason: The approach questions (tooth pain? red/bleeding/enlarged gums?) are partly flowchart routing and partly check items
elements.problem: Toothache, Gingival erythema, Bleeding gums and Gingival enlargement are all in check_for.
evidence: Check for urgent and likely gum/teeth conditions :: check_for (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Toothache" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Gingival erythema" "disorder")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Bleeding gums" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Gingival enlargement" "disorder"))

parts_missing: 'at gumline' location of the brown/black staining (Staining of tooth carries no site)
'pits' (only Cavity on tooth structure covers 'holes'; pits are arguably folded in)
elements.problem: Staining, holes and missing teeth are OR'd as the page intends. Missing teeth alone, or any tooth staining (not only brown/black at the gumline), gives probable caries. That follows the page literally but is broad.
evidence: Diagnose probable dental caries (gum/teeth symptoms) :: (or (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Staining of tooth" "disorder")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Cavity" "morphologic abnormality") (finding_site (snomed_concept "Tooth structure" "body structure"))) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Tooth absent" "finding")))

elements.scope_reason: 'May have tooth pain with hot or cold food/drink' is supportive, not a required criterion
parts_missing: tooth pain provoked by hot/cold food or drink (thermal sensitivity), as supporting caries evidence
elements.problem: Not encoded anywhere. Because the page says 'may have', leaving it out of the AND/OR logic is defensible. It could have been an OR'd supporting finding.
Red, bleeding and enlarged gums are OR'd, which is correct.
evidence: Diagnose probable gum problem (gum/teeth symptoms) :: (or (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Gingival erythema" "disorder")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Bleeding gums" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Gingival enlargement" "disorder")))

parts_missing: 'Previous' tooth pain: the rule needs Toothache to be recorded, so a patient whose pain has settled but who has pus and swelling will not get the diagnosis
elements.problem: Pus in mouth is Pus (morphologic abnormality) on Oral cavity structure, which is acceptable. Current toothache is encoded and AND'd.
evidence: Diagnose probable dental abscess (gum/teeth symptoms) :: (and (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Toothache" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Pus" "morphologic abnormality") (finding_site (snomed_concept "Oral cavity structure" "body structure"))) ...)

elements.problem: Swelling next to tooth is encoded as a third AND'd condition. The page's comma ('pus in mouth, swelling next to tooth') could also be read as OR. AND is the stricter and plausible reading.
evidence: Diagnose probable dental abscess (gum/teeth symptoms) :: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Swelling" "finding") (finding_site (snomed_concept "Tooth, gum, and/or supporting structure" "body structure")))

elements.scope_reason: 'Dental caries likely' conclusion; the advise/refer bullets are management
evidence: Diagnose probable dental caries (gum/teeth symptoms) :: (diagnosis (snomed_concept "Dental caries" "disorder") probable)

elements.scope_reason: 'Gum problem likely' conclusion; the rest is management
elements.problem: 'Gum problem' maps to Gingival disease (disorder), the closest general concept.
evidence: Diagnose probable gum problem (gum/teeth symptoms) :: (diagnosis (snomed_concept "Gingival disease" "disorder") probable)

elements.problem: The refer-to-dentist criteria (no better after 5 days, foul breath, swollen gums, temperature >= 38 °C, mobile teeth, bone loss, HIV/diabetes) only drive a non-urgent referral, not triage or a diagnosis.

elements.scope_reason: 'Dental abscess likely' conclusion; the drugs and referrals are management
elements.problem: The diagnosis is encoded. 'Refer urgently if worse, temperature >= 38 °C or no better after 2 days' and 'refer same day if > 65, alcohol/drug misuse, HIV, diabetes' are follow-up and referral escalation, so they are treated as management and are not encoded. That is acceptable under the no-manage rule, though arguably a priority escalation.
evidence: Diagnose probable dental abscess (gum/teeth symptoms) :: (diagnosis (snomed_concept "Dental abscess" "disorder") probable)

rule_level_problems.rule: Check for urgent and likely gum/teeth conditions / Urgent: gum/teeth symptoms with danger signs
rule_level_problems.problem: The trigger and the complaint conjunct are the grouper concepts 'Tooth finding' and 'Gingivae finding'. Evidence matching is by exact s-expression, so unless the engine applies is_a subsumption, recording Toothache, Bleeding gums or Unable to eat will not satisfy them. The check task may never fire, and the Urgent rule would need a literal 'Tooth finding' record. Toothache and Bleeding gums are is_a children of these groupers, so this works only with subsumption.
A three-way AND of current Toothache + pus + swelling misses the page's 'previous' tooth pain, and is stricter than a possible OR reading of 'pus in mouth, swelling next to tooth'.
A single OR'd 'Tooth absent' or any 'Staining of tooth' gives probable caries. This is literal to the page but drops the 'brown/black at gumline' specificity.

summary: The red box is encoded faithfully: temperature >= 38 °C AND face/jaw/tooth swelling, unable to eat/drink, and spontaneous or night tooth pain, all at Urgent with check_for coverage. All three 'likely' diagnoses are present. The most consequential risk is that the complaint anchor uses the grouper concepts 'Tooth finding' / 'Gingivae finding', which fire only if the engine applies subsumption. Smaller issues: the abscess rule ignores 'previous' tooth pain, and caries omits gumline/pits and thermal-sensitivity pain.
